summary: This Best Current Practice document removes a limit on the number of Area Directors who manage an IETF Area. It updates RFC 2026 and RFC 2418.

eli5.summary: The IETF used to say an area could have at most two directors. This removes that limit, so more can be appointed if needed.

questions: how many area directors can an ietf area have
subtitle: Lets the IETF define an Area as managed by one or more Area Directors instead of one or two.

tldr.problem: The IETF's definition of an Area said it is managed by one or two Area Directors, which conflicted with an IESG proposal for an Area with three.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC replaces "one or two" with "one or more" in RFC 2026 and RFC 2418.
tldr.outcome: The IESG gains flexibility in organizing the IETF's work, though the change is not meant to grow the IESG significantly.

today: RFC 7475 is a Best Current Practice and has not been obsoleted. It updates RFC 2026 and RFC 2418.

sections.title: Scope and Intent
sections.content: The RFC updates RFC 2026 (BCP 9) to remove the limit on how many Area Directors manage an Area, and updates RFC 2418 (BCP 25) to match. The aim is to give the IESG more flexibility. It does not change the role of an Area and does not argue that more than two Area Directors is optimal in the long run. If several Areas need more than two, the IESG should consider other ways of organizing the work.
sections.eli5: This is a small rule change to give the leaders some room, not a plan to add lots of captains.

sections.title: Why the Change
sections.content:
The IESG had explored splitting and combining Areas, and one proposal produced a single Area with three Area Directors. That conflicted with the old wording. Recent IESGs had two per Area except the General Area, but the number has varied since RFC 1396. In 1996 the IESG placed three Area Directors in one Area, and in 1999 it last increased the number, asking the Nominating Committee for a second Area Director in the Routing Area.

The requirement of RFC 7437 that the Nominating Committee review about half the IESG positions each year is unchanged.
sections.eli5: Sometimes a team really did have three captains in the past, so the rule just caught up with real life.

sections.title: The Text Change
sections.content:
In RFC 2026, "An Area is managed by one or two Area Directors" becomes "one or more Area Directors". In RFC 2418, "Each IETF area is managed by one or two Area Directors (ADs)" becomes "one or more". Informational documents such as RFC 3710 that say "one or two" should be considered updated.

The RFC says it has no direct Internet security implications.
sections.eli5: Two words change: "one or two" becomes "one or more".
